families.family_description: OH-rich biopolymer/film matrices combined with retained proton donors and optional plasticised phases target cold-flexible, hydrogen-bonded transport networks.
descriptor_match: D2: DES or retained polar phases support bound-fluid continuity at low temperature.
D3: biopolymer/PVA-like matrices are analogously suited to avoid brittle channel disconnection when plasticised.
D6: starch, chitosan, and PVA all supply dense OH-rich proton-relay landscapes.
D7: chitosan and low-loaded phosphoric-acid strategies support conducting-phase retention.

families.family_description: Tubular or fibrous inorganic hosts embedded in polymeric scaffolds can confine and align hydrated acid domains for stable proton pathways.
descriptor_match: D4: phosphoric-acid or acid-complex environments can remain non-crystallising under confinement or DES-like association.
D5: attapulgite, halloysite, and analogous nanofillers provide interconnected confinement and channel guidance.
D7: clay hosts are explicitly linked to acid immobilisation and reduced leaching.
D6: retained phosphoric acid supplies proton-relay functionality within the confined network.

families.family_description: Amorphous phosphate-rich networks offer intrinsically continuous proton-conducting domains with strong hydrogen-bond participation and high retention.
descriptor_match: D1: protonated phosphate glass is directly described as an amorphous continuous transport medium.
D6: phosphate glasses provide strong hydrogen-bond-mediated proton mobility.
D7: the conducting phase is structurally retained in the glass network, though durability can be conditional.
D3: amorphous glass avoids liquid freezing but may trade against low-temperature mechanical compliance.
